SUBJECT: APPEAL OF THE DIRECTOR OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT'S DECISION TO
DENY AN EXTENSION OF TEMPORARY USE PERMIT NO. 2020-01 FOR TRUCK TRAILER
STORAGE AT 8530 ALAMEDA STREET.

PURPOSE: Public hearing to consider an appeal of the Director of Community Development's decision to deny
an extension of Temporary Use Pe1mit (TUP) No. 2020-01 for truck-trailer storage at 8530 Alameda Street, South
Gate.

RECOMMENDED ACTION:
1. CONDUCT a public heating pursuant to South Gate Municipal Code Table 11.51-1 and Section 11.50.040.B;
2. ACCEPT the dete1mination that this matter is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act;
3. ADOPT the findings as outlined in Resolution No. 2023-02 (Attachment A); and
4. UPHOLD the decision of the Director of Community Development denying an extension of TUP No. 2020-
  01 by adopting Resolution No. 2023-05.

PUBLIC NOTIFICATION: Advertising and notification of the public heating for this item was conducted in
compliance with Sections 11.50.020 and 11.50.030 of the South Gate Municipal Code ("SGMC"). Notices of the
hearing were posted and published in the "South Gate Press" on February 9, April 6 and April 20, 2023.

ENVIRONMENTAL EVALUATION: The California Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA"), codified at
California Public Resources Code§§ 21000 et seq., requires the City to consider the potential environmental
impacts of any project which the City is asked to approve. State regulations known as the "CEQA Guidelines",
codified at Division 6 of Title 14 of the California Code of Regulations, provide a number of "categorical
exemptions" for activities which are not deemed to be projects under CEQA or which are otherwise not subject
to CEQA. In the present case, the matter before the City Council is exempt from CEQA pursuant to a Class l
exemption set forth in Section 15301 of the CEQA Guidelines. Class 1 exemptions apply to the operation, repair,
maintenance, permitting, leasing, licensing, or minor alteration of existing public or private structures, facilities,
mechanical equipment, or topographical features, involving negligible or no expansion of existing or fo1mer use.
Here, the Planning Commission is being asked to approve or deny a license to continue the existing or former use
of the licensed facility and is therefore a matter covered by the Class l exception.

BACKGROUND: This is an appeal by Jason Engle on behalf of Alameda Engle Properties, LLC, the owner of
property located at 8530 Alameda Street. Mr. Engle is appealing the Director of Community Development's
decision to deny an extension or renewal of Temporary Use Permit 2020-01. The history of that Temporary Use
Permit is as follows:

The City's Business License Department shows business license records (Attachment B) for "Jack Engle Co,"
which statted business on Ap1il 18, 1977, and closed business on March 27, 2020, at 8530 Alameda Street. This
business type was listed as a "Manufacturing - Metal" business with "outside storage only." The appellant and
its predecessor had previously been utilizing the property to operate a metal recycling facility, in addition to the
ancillary storage of truck containers and truck trailers.

Upon closing that business, the appellant continued to utilize the site by leasing the prope1ty to tenants for the  6
 outside  storage  of truck  trailers  and tiuck  containers.  In order to do so, the applicant  applied  for, and received,
Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01.  That permit  "permitted  the use of truck trailer  storage  for a one year period  with
possible  one year extensions  up to a maximum  period  of five years from  the date of approval,  at 8530 Alameda
Street,"  with  six conditions  of approval.  A July  16, 2020  letter  from  the City's  former  Director  of Community
Development,  setting  forth  those conditions  of approval  for that pertnit,  is attached  hereto  as Attachment  C. As
of the appeal date, the appellant  has failed  to comply  with  the required  conditions  of approval  and has also been
operating  without  a city business  license.

The  appellant  applied  for  a "renewal"  of Temporary  Use Permit  2020-01  on July  11, 2022.  For the reasons
explained  below,  the City's  current  Director  of Community  Development  declined  to renew  the permit.  This
appeal  followed.  The City  Manager's  January  12, 2023  letter  to the appellant,  and the appellant's  January  26,
2023 letter in response,  both pertain  to that appeal  and are attached  here to as Attachment  D and Attachment  E.

ANALYSIS:  The renewal  application  was denied  because under  the SGMC:  (1) the use which  is the subject  of
the  Temporary  Use  Permit  is prohibited  at 8530  Alameda;  and (2) Temporary  Use Permits  can only  allow
otherwise  unauthorized  uses to be conducted  for a few days, not for multi-year  periods.

Past/Proposed  Use of Property  is as a "Truck  Storage/Terminal":  Applicant  and its tenant  have been using  the
subject  property  to store trucks,  truck-trailers,  and storage  containers.  Under  the SGMC,  this use is defined  as
"truck  storage/terminal"  use which,  pursuant  to the SGMC  Section  11.60.230  "T"  definitions,  "means  indoor  or
outdoor  site for freight,  truck  terminals,  truck  storage  yards,  or similar  commercial  facilities."

SGMC  Prohibits  that Use at 8530 Alameda  Street:  The subject  property  is zoned  Industrial  Flex  (IF).  Table
11.21-3,  under  SGMC  Section  11.21.030  "Land  use pernnissions  tables",  lists  allowed  land uses within  the IF
zone. Truck  storage/teiminal  use is not listed  on that Table  as an allowed  use within  the IF zone.  SGMC  Section
11.21.020  notes that "Any  land use that is not specifically  listed in the land use tables for the applicable  zone shall
not be allowed  or permitted  within  the zone."  Therefore,  the storage  of trucks,  truck-trailers  and containers  is a
prohibited  use in the IF zone.

Temporary  Use Pertnits  Cannot  Authorize  Prohibited  Uses for Extended  Durations.  Pursuant  to SGMC  Section
11.51.070  "Temporary  Use Permit,"  temporary  use permits  are processed  administratively  to "allow  for short-
term  activities  that warrant  individual  consideration  and are acceptable  because  of their  temporary,  short-tertn
nature."  SGMC  Section  11.51.070  (A) "Temporary  Uses,"  also notes  that the "provisions  of this section  shall
regulate  all special  events  and temporary  land  uses as permitted  by Table  11.21-3,  11.21-4,  or 11.21-5,  as
applicable  to the zone, or as determined  by the director."  SGMC  Section  11.51.010  (B) lists "Mandatory  Approval
Conditions"  for temporary  use permits,  wherein  there are "limits  on the maximum  duration  will  be specified  in
the permit,  and shall not exceed three days in a row,  or ten working  days in any calendar  year."

Original  Issuance  of the TUP was Done in Error,  and Renewal  of the TUP is not authorized  by the SGMC.  Based
on the aforementioned  reasoning,  the City's  current  Director  of Community  Development  determined  that the
City  would  not grant  an extension  of TUP 2020-01.  That Temporary  Use Permit  should  never have been issued
in the first place,  since it purported  to authorize  the subject  use for one or more years,  far longer  than the three-
consecutive-day  and ten-nonconsecutive-day  maximum  periods  authorized  by the SGMC.  The Director  and the
City  Manager  each communicated  that decision  to the appellant.  Appellant  has appealed  that decision,  which
appeal is the subject  of the above-referenced  hearing.

  7
 CONCLUSION: Staff believes the Director's decision to deny the applicant's request to extend Temporary Use
Permit 2020-01 is mandated by the SGMC. Staff recommends that the Planoing Commission uphold the
Director's decision and deny the appellant's request.

ATTACHMENTS: A. Resolution No. 2023-05
  B. Business license records
  C. Temporary Use Permit 2020-01 approval letter, dated July 16, 2020
  D. City Manager's letter, dated January 12, 2023
  E. Appellant's letter, dated January 26, 2023

   RESOLUTION NO. 2023-05

  A RESOLUTION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE
  CITY OF SOUTH GATE, STATE OF CALIFORNIA, UPHOLDING
  THE DIRECTOR OF COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT’S
  DECISION TO DENY AN EXTENSION OF TEMPORARY USE
  PERMIT NO. 2020-01 FOR TRUCK TRAILER STORAGE AT 8530
  ALAMEDA STREET

  WHEREAS, the Applicant and property owner, Jason Engle on behalf of Alameda Engle
Properties, LLC, requested an extension of Temporary Use Permit 2020-01 to allow for the
continued use of truck trailer and container storage at 8530 Alameda Street, a use which is
prohibited at that location by the South Gate Municipal Code (“SGMC”); and

  WHEREAS, the Director of Community Development denied the extension request of
Temporary Use Permit 2020-01, based on evidence and testimony provided by the Applicant and
City records and provisions of the SGMC pertaining to the duration of temporary use permits; and

  WHEREAS, the Applicant filed an Appeal of the Director’s Decision on the ground that
the temporary use permit was previously approved and granted; and

  WHEREAS, pursuant to California Government Code Section 65854, the Planning
Commission duly noticed and agendized a public hearing and conducted the public hearing on this
matter on March 21, 2023 and April 18, 2023, and adopted Planning Commission Resolution No.
2023-05.

  WHEREAS, the Planning Commission made the following findings:

  1. The land use of storage of truck trailers and containers is not authorized or allowed by
  the South Gate Municipal Code on any land within the Industrial Flex (IF) zone, of
  which the subject property is a part.

  2. Temporary Use Permit 2020-01 was originally issued in error and in violation of City
  ordinances. Temporary use permits are to be used for “short-term activities” which are
  of a “short-term nature.” In addition, the South Gate Municipal Code specifies that the
  maximum duration of a temporary use permit shall not exceed three days in a row, or
  ten working days in any calendar year. Temporary Use Permit 2020-01 was issued in
  error as the approval was granted for a longer period of time than the South Gate
  Municipal Code allows for.

  NOW, THEREFORE, THE PLANNING COMMISSION OF THE CITY OF
SOUTH GATE, CALIFORNIA, HEREBY RESOLVES AS FOLLOWS:

  SECTION 1. The Planning Commission hereby finds that all of the facts set forth in the
Recitals of this Resolution are true and correct.

  SECTION 2. The Planning Commission hereby finds that the subject decision is exempt
from the California Environment Quality Act of 1970 (“CEQA”), because it can be seen with
certainty that this decision has no likelihood of causing a significant negative effect on the

  9
 environment and the effects derivative from the decision are exempt from the application of
CEQA, pursuant to a Class 1 exemption under Section 15301 of the State CEQA Guidelines (15
Cal.Code Regs. § 15301).

  SECTION 3. The Planning Commission of the City of South Gate, pursuant to the facts
noted above, does hereby uphold the decision of the Director of Community Development to deny
an extension of Temporary Use Permit 2020-01 at 8530 Alameda Street.

This action was adopted by the following vote at the Planning Commission meeting of April 18,
2023.

Dear Messrs.  Otting  and Martinez,

We are in receipt  of Mr. Martinez's  December  23, 2022,  e-mail  addressed  to the South Gate City
Manager,  the City's  Director  of Community  Development  ("Director"),  and certain  members  of
the City  Council.  We understand  that Mr. Martinez's  e-mail  is intended  as a notice  to the City that
Fleet  Yards  Inc, wishes  to appeal  the Director's  denial  of your  request  for  an extension  of the
above-referenced  Temporary  Use Permit.  Such appeals  should  be filed  along with  the appropriate
fees required  under the adopted  fee schedule  with the City Clerk  pursuant  to South Gate Municipal
Code ("SGMC")  {S)11.50.040.  Those  appeals,  including  fees, according  to the SGMC,  are to be
submitted  within  10 working  days of the decision  notification.  Given  the holidays,  I am extending
that time period  for the applicant  to Januaiy  30, 2023,  at 5:00 PM.

The fees to be paid are the Appeal  fee ($2,364)  and the Public  Notice  fee ($1,570)  for a total  of
$3,934.  In addition,  there should  be a written  letter  signed  by the property  owner  or authorized
officer/agent  of the property  owner  requesting  the appeal.  In that appeal letter,  the property  owner
should  clearly  state what  they are appealing  and provide  any supporting  documents  they wish  to
submit  for the Planning  Commission  to review  as part of the appeal.  If a written  appeal letter  and
fees are submitted  on or before  Januaiy  30, 2023, you will  be notified  of the date, time and location
of the appeal  hearing  before  the Planning  Commission,  in accordance  with  SGMC  §§ 11.50.020

the Director's  decision  being  finalized  and in effect.

At  the  hearing,  the  Director  will  be recommending  that  the  Planning  Commission  uphold  the
Director's  decision  to deny  the renewal  of the subject  pernnit,  for the following  reasons:

  1.  The  truck-trailer  storage  use that  is the subject  of the permit  is not  authorized  or
  allowed  by the SGMC  on any land within  the Industrial  Flex  (IF)  zone of which  the
  subject  property  is a part.  Table  11.21-3  shows  that  outside  storage  of vehicles  is
  not permitted  in the IF zone.

  2.  The  permit  was  originally  issued  in  error  and  in violation  of  City  ordinances.
  SGMC  {§ 11.51.070.A  states  that temporary  use pernnits  are to be used  for "short-
  term  activities"  which  are  of  a "short-term  nature".  SGMC  §  11.51.070.B.4
  specifies  that  the maximum  duration  of a temporary  use permit  shall  not  exceed
  three  days  in a row,  or ten working  days  in any  calendar  year.  This  means  that
  when  the former  City  official  issued  his July  16, 2020,  letter  purporting  to approve
  a temporary  use permit  having  an initial  term  of one year  and four  potential  annual
  extensions  thereafter,  that  approval  was void  because  it was issued  in violation  of
  the limitations  imposed  by the SGMC.  That  official  had no authority  to issue  the
  permit,  and Fleet  Yards  Inc.  had no right  to rely  on the permit.

I would  note,  that  under  an appeal  of a land  use entitlement,  the burden  is upon  the applicant  to
show  the decision  by the Director  to be not consistent  with  or is a wrong  interpretation  of the South
Gate  Municipal  Code  and  thus,  the  reason  why  the  Planning  Commission  should  alter  that
decision.  In this situation,  the burden  will  be on the applicant  to demonstrate:

  1.  That  the  South  Gate  Municipal  Code  11.51.070  pernnits  temporary  uses  longer  than

  The Doctrine of Equitable Estoppel was designed to promote fair and equitable
business transactions. The doctrine is based on the principle that a party who has
made a promise should be held accountable for it where reliance on the agreement was
reasonable, and enforcement of the agreement is necessary to avoid injustice.
Drennan v. Star Paving Co. (1958) 51 Cal.2d 409, 412-413; Garcia v. World Sav. &
Loan Assn. (2010) 183 Cal.App.4th 1031,1037. Here, Fleet Yards only agreed to the
TUP as a demonstration of good faith and willingness to work with the City regarding its
vision for the community. Based on communications from City staff on July 8, 2020, in
addition to the plain language of the TUP, the City was to consider additional extensions
of the TUP in addition to the initial five-year term. In addition, both AEP and Fleet Yards
agreed to the TUP as a measure of good faith and willingness to work with the City. It is
inequitable for the City to renege on this agreement. AEP forwent multiple lucrative
opportunities to sell the Property in reliance on the City’s communications and the
reasonable expectation that the City’s permits, licenses, and representations are
consistent notwithstanding changes in staff, changes in departmental priorities, and
unilateral changes to the zoning code. If the City does not honor its prior commitments,
both AEP and Fleet Yards will suffer substantial financial harm. In addition, this
inconsistency in City policies discourages investment in our community and is a
substantial deviation from the City’s treatment of similarly situated legacy businesses.

  4. Conclusion

  For the reasons stated above, the equitable path forward is to acknowledge truck
trailer storage on the Property as a preserved, legal nonconforming use in light of the
substantial evidence supporting this finding, and the requirements of the General Plan.
In the alternative, we respectfully request that the City reverse the Director’s denial of
the TUP extension. We understand that the City’s position is that the TUP was issued in
error. However, where, as here, immediately terminating the TUP causes substantial
harm to the community, and there is substantial evidence supporting that the use is
legal and nonconforming, we urge you to use this opportunity to make it right. As a
further demonstration of good faith and willingness to work together, we respectfully
request the City share any documentation indicating that the truck trailer storage is not
authorized pursuant to the legacy operations on the Property, and procedures for
obtaining a business permit zoning clearance where, as here, the use is legal
nonconforming.

History:

  managing affairs.

  operation.
  •  We are environmentally conscientious with water monitoring wells, dust recovery
  systems and we are working with SCE to build an energy efficient building (Savings By
  Design). We are currently enrolled in a voluntary program to save energy by shutting
  down equipment during peak hours.
  •  We employ 62 people in Los Angeles County, some of whom have been here since we
  opened.
  •  We are by definition an environmentally friendly, sustainable, recycling business that
  process and recycles metal for reuse.
  •  We are not open to the public. Our suppliers are industrial customers who generate large
  volumes of metal recyclable products.

  •  New building plans are complete. We have been through entire approval process with

  •  We have been in temporary offices for 18 months.
  •  Los Angeles County has suggested that South Gate annex the portion of our property
  which resides in LA.
  •  LA County will not allow a sewer connection because the existing private sewer line
  crossed more than one lot line.

Concerns:
  • Timing

  • Permit Process: will we have to start from scratch?

To the Attention of Chris Jeffers:

This letter shall serve as notice to the City of South Gate, that Alameda Engle Properties would like to
appeal the “City of South Gate’s Denial of Request by Fleet Yards Inc. for Extension of Temporary Use
Permit No. TUP 2020-01 for Truck-Trailer Storage at 8530 Alameda Street.” Accompanying this letter is a
check for $3,934, which is comprised of $2,364 (Appeal Fee) and $1,570 (Public Notice Fee).

For over 50 years, the subject property has been Heavy Industrial and has been Truck Storage,
Container/Trailer Storage, as well as a Metal Recycling Facility. Since the previous tenant (Jack Engle
and Company) has vacated the property, it has remained in similar utilization (less the Truck Storage
and Recycling operation). Upon the previous tenant departure, we inquired within the city of South
Gate for a reduced utilization. Although we felt we didn’t need to “check” with the city of South Gate,
we did, as we have always maintained a good relationship, being on the property for over 50 years in
Heavy Industrial. Since ownership of the property, no vehicle/container that moves in or out of the
property does so through South Gate. All movements are through Los Angeles, as the exit/entrance on
Alameda Street is a right turn only; heading away from the city of South Gate. Further to this, the
property and its content are not visible from the street, as the property is surrounded by a 10-foot solid
wall and then is offset further from Alameda Street due to the Alameda Corridor and ACTA owned land.
Further to this, the current tenant has done community outreach events to build good repour with the
community.

Upon bringing in a new tenant, we requested our item/situation to be brought before the City Council
for a permanent solution to the matter but the Community Development Director, Joe Perez, chose to
employ a TUP. This TUP had extensions that renewed yearly. The current tenant lease was based upon
the Temporary Use Permit No. TUP2020-01 8530 Alameda Street (APN 6202-036-003). Why the
Community Development Director chose a TUP with the noted conditions, was not our place, although
we disagreed because we wanted the item brought to the City Council for approval. However, it was
the permitting decision of the City. We are asking the City to continue with its signed contract, as many
factors were put into motion based upon that document. Maybe the renewal should not be called a
TUP, but it should reflect the 50+ years this property was Heavy Industrial and continue with the
longtime usage of its past. Please see at the end of this letter the original document drawn-up to

  328
 denote all our points that are consistent and relevant for this appeal. Hence, there is nothing different
then versus now.

It is clear thru current written and verbal communication that the City of South Gate wants to rectify a
mistake and/or wrongdoing by its previous employee (Joe Perez, Community Development Director).
The City is within its full right to do so, but ask that the City of South Gate take a more humble and
welcoming approach and do everything possible within reason, to work with us rather than punish us
for an action that the City officially took.

This current reversal of a previously signed City document feels like discrimination of the landowner
and seems to favor the bigger name companies that make use of Heavy Industrial for the same
practice. The City has no solutions, just reversal of a previous decision. A decision to which (right or
wrong), was decided by the Community Development Director of the City of South Gate with signing
authority. Once again, if the City of South Gate wants to rectify a mistake and/or wrong-doing by its
previous employee (Joe Perez, Community Development Director), the City is within its full right to do
so, but we ask that this is done in a collaborative way that is mutually beneficial and allows us to
continue to use the property in the way it has been for over 50 years.

Currently, this same type of Container Storage is within the City of South Gate, and we are asking for no
different treatment. This takes place at the following location:
JB Hunt MT Lot Ardine - 5 Acres
4500 Ardine St, South Gate, CA 90280

Denying the previously signed City document, the City is not allowing the property to be utilized. This is
ignoring the Grandfathered status. Alameda Engle Properties has a desire to engage the City of South

been a part of the community at its current locations since 1963. Approximately 6.77 acres of the property of
the Company is located in the City of South Gate and the remaining approximately 2.947 acres, known as 8440

WHEREAS, for over 50 years, Company has continuously been operating as an Industrial Recycling Center
(wholesale-not open to public), which operation includes: trucking (pickup and deliveries), processing of
ferrous and non-ferrous materials (shredding, bailing, shearing, sorting, and picking), and includes container

which have resulted in, among other matters, making the property on which Company owns and operates its
